outcome: Time from catheter insertion to delivery
cohort: 177 term pregnant women (nulliparous and multiparous) aged 18 to 50 years old with a Bishop score of <6 and cervical dilation of <2 cm undergoing induction of labor
finding: Induction of labor with a single-balloon catheter and oxytocin with planned removal of the catheter at 6 hours, rather than 12 hours, resulted in a shorter time from insertion to delivery without increasing the rate of cesarean delivery.
